project.name: lq-skills
project.description: Curated collection of harness-agnostic agent skills for legal work built by the Legal Quants community (~100 lawyer-builders across 17+ jurisdictions) — transparent, version-controlled markdown skill definitions with evals, spanning jurisdiction-specific review, citation verification, and statutory analysis. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the root README to understand what LQ Skills is: a curated registry of harness-agnostic agent skills for legal work, built by the Legal Quants community of roughly 100 lawyer-builders across 17+ jurisdictions. The README's skill table maps every skill to its author, jurisdiction, and purpose, and the install instructions show the same skill folders working across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, and OpenClaw. Unlike a typical codebase, there is no runtime entry point here — the architecture is a library of self-contained skill folders, which this tour walks layer by layer.

tour.title: Anatomy of a Skill
tour.description: Every skill in this repo is a folder whose front door is a SKILL.md file — the entry-point layer the rest of the architecture hangs off. sgcite is the cleanest minimal example: a single markdown definition that tells an agent how to verify Singapore court citations against eLitigation, detect hallucinated cases, band its confidence, and escalate. Notice that the 'code' here is prose: the workflow, output format, and escalation rules are instructions an LLM agent executes, not functions a computer runs.
tour.languageLesson: Agent skills use YAML frontmatter (name, description) as the trigger contract — the harness reads it to decide when to load the skill — while the markdown body is the workflow the agent follows once loaded. One format, many harnesses.

tour.title: A Deep Skill: Privacy Navigator
tour.description: At the other end of the spectrum from sgcite sits us-state-privacy-navigator, the most connected node in the whole graph (38 incoming edges). Its SKILL.md is an orchestrator: intake, applicability triage across all 20 US state privacy laws, conflict-of-laws synthesis, gap analysis against enforcement precedent, and citation-audited memo deliverables. The skill README documents this hub-and-spoke design — one SKILL.md coordinating references, scripts, assets, and tests that the next several steps explore in turn.

tour.title: Reference Knowledge Bases
tour.description: SKILL.md workflows stay short because the domain law lives in per-skill reference corpora, loaded on demand only when a workflow step needs them. In the privacy navigator, the applicability matrix encodes consumer-count and revenue thresholds for every state law; per-state cards like California's (the deepest, covering CCPA/CPRA rights, GPC signals, and CPPA enforcement) carry statute-level detail; and workflow references like DSAR routing turn that law into step-by-step procedure. This is the repo's equivalent of a database layer: curated, citable legal knowledge instead of tables.

tour.title: The Review-Skill Pattern
tour.description: Document-review skills share a recurring reference pattern, and msa-review-saas is the tightest cluster in the graph: a SKILL.md plus four companion references that are always used together. The issue checklist defines tiered terms to inspect (liability caps, data ownership, SLAs), the red-flags file lists dealbreakers, the severity rubric standardizes how findings are rated, and the perspective lens recalibrates the whole review for vendor versus customer side. Spotting this checklist-rubric-lens triad will help you read the NDA, DPA, and purchase-MSA review skills at a glance — they follow the same shape.

tour.title: Worked Examples as Calibration
tour.description: Because skill output is prose, not typed return values, skills anchor expected tone and depth with worked examples under examples/ directories. enhance-prompt — a skill that rewrites vague legal prompts into structured ones — ships three: a short vague prompt fully expanded, a case where enhancement is correctly skipped, and an expansion that routes to another skill. These examples function like snapshot tests for LLM behavior: they show the agent (and the contributor) exactly what good output looks like before any quality gate runs.

tour.title: Templates and Structured Assets
tour.description: Skills that produce client-facing deliverables carry assets: fill-in scaffolding that keeps output consistent. The privacy navigator's memo template fixes the memorandum's skeleton — disclaimer, entity profile, per-state applicability matrix, gap log, remediation roadmap — while applicability-questions.json is a JSON Schema defining the structured intake whose answers drive the threshold tests. Reusable notice clauses round out the set. Note the division of labor: the LLM drafts judgment-laden analysis, but structure and intake are pinned down by templates and schemas from this layer.

tour.title: Automation Scripts
tour.description: Where a wrong answer is unacceptable, skills hand work to deterministic scripts that the agent executes rather than reads. The navigator's applicability_check.py evaluates the Step-7 intake against all 20 states' threshold tests and emits Applies / Likely Applies / Does Not Apply verdicts with reasoning; citation_audit.py blocks memos that contain uncited claims or malformed statutory citations; conflict_resolver.py and precedent_match.py handle cross-state conflicts and the 82-action enforcement corpus; and generate_docx_memo.js renders the final DOCX. This is the repo's core architectural bet: legal judgment goes to the LLM, threshold math and citation discipline go to code.
tour.languageLesson: These Python helpers follow a CLI contract: JSON in, JSON out, non-zero exit on failure. That makes them harness-agnostic too — any agent that can run a shell command can use them, with no SDK or import coupling.

tour.title: CoQuill: Multi-Agent Assembly
tour.description: CoQuill shows the most elaborate composition pattern in the repo: an orchestrator SKILL.md that runs a seven-phase document-assembly pipeline by delegating to three nested sub-skills, each pairing its own SKILL.md with a script. The analyzer's analyze.py extracts Jinja2 variables, conditionals, and loops from a docx/HTML/markdown template into a manifest; the renderer's render.py fills the template into docx, HTML, or markdown; and the transcriber's transcribe.py converts the finished interview session into a human-readable record. It is the same prose-plus-script architecture from Step 8, scaled up into a pipeline of cooperating agents.

tour.title: CoQuill Template Packs
tour.description: CoQuill's templates layer makes Step 9 concrete. Each example pack pairs a template body — the meeting-notes markdown, the CC-BY-licensed Bonterms Mutual NDA docx, an HTML invoice with print styling — with a machine-generated manifest.yaml cataloguing its variables, types, and conditional groups, plus an optional author-supplied config.yaml that overrides labels, interview questions, and defaults. The three bodies deliberately exercise all three render paths from the renderer script, doubling as worked examples for template authors.
tour.languageLesson: Jinja2 placeholders ({{ variable }}, {% if %}, {% for %}) work identically across docx, HTML, and markdown bodies. The generated manifest.yaml is machine truth about what the template needs; the hand-written config.yaml layers human intent (labels, question wording, defaults) on top without touching the template.

tour.title: Testing the Deterministic Core
tour.description: The scripts from Step 8 are real software, so they get real tests: run_all.py discovers every test module via stdlib unittest and exits non-zero on any failure, making the suite CI-friendly with no dependencies. test_applicability_check.py drives the threshold engine with fixtures like a multistate intake profile, while test_citation_audit.py proves the auditor catches the seeded errors in memo_with_errors.md. The fixtures encode the contract: given this exact intake, the engine must reach these exact per-state verdicts.

tour.title: Behavioral Evals for Prose Skills
tour.description: Most skills have no Python to unit-test — their behavior is prose — so the repo adds a second quality gate: lightweight behavioral evals. The evals/ README explains the harness: per-skill evals.yaml files define scenarios and assertions about the agent's output, like uk-citation-verification's requirement that a live-source check actually names its sources. Skills authored against an acceptance bar also carry a test-plan.md, like enhance-prompt's six-scenario corpus plan, mirroring for LLM behavior what Step 11's fixtures do for code.
tour.languageLesson: Evals-as-YAML is the emerging test format for agent skills: each scenario lists an input prompt plus assertions about the response (required elements, prohibited behaviors). They are graded by inspection or by a judge model rather than asserted by code.

tour.title: Governance and Contribution
tour.description: The final layer is what keeps a 40-plus-skill, multi-author registry coherent. CONTRIBUTING.md sets the practitioner-built philosophy, the fork-and-PR process, and the required SKILL.md-plus-references format you have now seen throughout the tour; ACCESS-MODES.md is the repo-wide policy that skills must never assume tool or credential access, since the same skill may run in harnesses with very different capabilities; and PR-READINESS.md is the pre-flight checklist covering content hygiene and cross-harness install checks. Together they explain how everything from sgcite's one file to the privacy navigator's full stack lands in one consistent library.
